dedupe_keys.name: yearly simulation of the dutch national railway timetable with opentrack prorail and haskoning 2014 to present

description: Since 2014 the engineering consultancy Haskoning has simulated the whole Dutch railway network for ProRail, the national rail infrastructure manager, to test the robustness of the national timetable before it runs. The Netherlands has one of the busiest networks in Europe, and growing passenger numbers, new stations and strict punctuality requirements leave small margins, so an infeasible timetable quickly spreads delays. Haskoning built a detailed microscopic model in OpenTrack containing all infrastructure, rolling stock, timetables and operational constraints, including future projects. Each year the new timetable is run through the model; time-distance diagrams and further analyses show bottlenecks, delays and interactions between trains on every route, and scenarios such as speed restrictions, planned works or new stations can be recomputed quickly. The study covers the national network, with attention to the busiest corridors and nodes. The case is described on Haskoning's project page, which is free to read online; the model and results are not available to the public. Outcome: planners at ProRail receive reports, graphs and concrete timetable adjustments each year, which the consultancy says strengthen network robustness and punctuality. Limitations: no quantified evaluation is published. The case shows operational capacity planning and resilience testing of a national rail timetable with a microscopic simulator, and uses the OpenTrack model catalogued here; ProRail's open track geometry is catalogued separately.
